review_headline: Gift Cards for all occasions - excellent!!  Five Granny Gems!!
review_body:
Easy to purchase, fast delivery, and perfect for my grandchild who lives on the opposite coast from me and is computer literate so she can happily do her own shopping! I buy these for birthday and Christmas gifts each year. Those reviews that complained there wasn't a message included with the gift card are half right. No, it isn't printed on the card or signed by anyone, but I tested this by typing my birthday message and having it mailed to me first, before sending it onward. There WAS a small (4x4 approx.) white piece of paper that had my exact message printed on it, but it was tossed into the cardboard box loosely, and could easily be missed by someone who wasn't looking for it specifically. It comes with a very nice sturdy gift card and envelope suitable for mailing.
I usually order the card to my home first, and then write a hand-written personal note on the card before mailing it to the recipient. Since they never expire, I like to pick them up as my budget allows throughout the year to have ready for that special occasion.
Update: 12-06-16 - I order these every year for Christmas and/or birthday gifts for my grandchildren. Their ages range from 12 to 22 and they love to choose what they want on Amazon.com and I don't have to stress over the sales or figure out what they would like. They love the freedom of choosing what they want, and often wait until the "after Christmas sales" to buy what they've had their eye on. I give this FIVE Granny Gems!

product_title: Amazon Gift Card - Print - Merry Christmas (Birds)
review_body: What is it? The name says it all really: It's a gift certificate that you purchase on line from Amazon, and print out at home. You can select from a range of graphic designs, set your nominated gift value, though Amazon defaulted to a generous $100, and include a text message of your own devising.  Is it good? Well it's just a gift certificate; it doesn't have a great deal of intrinsic reviewable property of its own. It's the gift you give when you can't think of, or be bothered to think of, an individual gift. As an example of its kind, it's neither special or unique. It's not unusually good  nor bad. It's just a gift certificate.  The only negative aspect to the thing is a comment some days later from a recipient, who told me that they appreciated their gift but couldn't work out how to redeem it. I think this is more likely to be related to the recipient than any inherent complication or mystery with the certificate itself.  So, why only three stars? It's not special or outstanding in any way, nor unusually flawed. It's just your run of the mill gift certificate.
